hooks.description: HARD BLOCK: the ontology plane may be written only where this bundle's DATA pipeline has reached its declared exit - a named human's sign-off at governance/data_plane_approval.yaml. A bundle declaring one pipeline keeps the legacy rule: default-DENY, lifted by the operator's .ontology-unlocked marker. The sign-off, the marker and the lock's own two halves (.claude/hooks/**, .claude/settings*.json) are denied UNCONDITIONALLY - no marker lifts them, because an unlock the agent can also satisfy is not a gate.

DETECTION, NOT CLOSURE - and stated that way on purpose. Scans the command for a write verb (>, >>, touch, tee, cp, mv, dd, ln, sed -i, perl -i, truncate, install, rsync, python -c, cat) beside a literal protected path, and denies. A constructed path, a base64'd one, a heredoc written to a script and then executed, or `cd` plus a relative path all walk past it. The permissions.deny block above raises the cost again without closing the class. Real authorization is out-of-band: CODEOWNERS on the sign-off path plus a review the agent holds no token for. The honest claim is detected-and-blocked, authorized out-of-band. NOTE: permissions.deny path-rule syntax varies by host version; the hook is the enforcement that does not depend on it.
